correctness.rationale: With r>=2 and m>=1 the hub-free flip graph is the Cartesian product of m stars K_{1,r}; the hub state couples only to the vacuum v. Each star has eigenvalues ±sqrt(r) and r-1 zero eigenvalues, and its vacuum sees only the two nonzero eigenvectors with equal weights. Tensoring gives the Laurent-coefficient nullity and the binomial vacuum measure. In the bordered kernel equations Ax+av=0 and <v,x>=0, projection to ker A forces a=0 exactly in the even case, when one peripheral zero direction is removed. In the odd case v is orthogonal to ker A and <v,A^+v>=0 by symmetry of the vacuum measure, so the orthogonal added kernel direction is h-A^+v and its normalization gives the stated hub weight. The proof's 'unique normalized zero vector' is understood as the unique bright direction orthogonal to the dark zero space; arbitrary mixtures with dark vectors can also overlap the hub. For odd m the residual spectral weight is <1/2, giving the all-time lower bound. For even m, with a=sqrt(p_m), z=P_0v/a and D=A^+v, the trajectory cos(at)(h-D)-i sin(at)z has initial error ||D|| and integrated residual ||D|| at pi/(2a); its hub component vanishes there. This proves the stated upper bound, not an exact minimum. The binomial local limit with a uniform central-mass bound allows dominated convergence against k^-2; the two reciprocal-square sums over odd and nonzero even k are pi^2/4 and pi^2/12. Stirling gives the claimed m^(1/4) time scale. The proof covers m=1 and fixed r in the asymptotic statements.
residual_risks: The finite spectrum and return tests use floating point and do not replace the exact proof. No robustness claim for detuning or noise is certified.
